title: POC weekly — model pinning & fallback matrix
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results for candidate models, confirm version pinning strategy, and define fallback/rollback matrix. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, KV/prefix cache behavior, and security concerns for VPC deployment. Agreed on end-to-end benchmark run and a rollback drill next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): All right, welcome back everyone. This is our weekly POC sync, 11/03. We'll try to keep it tight — around an hour. Quick round table?
[00:12] Samir (Cobalt): Hey Alex, hey Priya, thanks. We ran the batch tests overnight. Got some numbers — "
[00:18] Priya (Redwood): Great, Samir. Do you want to start with the latency tail or the cost numbers first?
[00:22] Samir (Cobalt): Latency. We pushed 1k concurrent short-chat requests — median looked fine, but p95 spiked when we hit long context. p95 about 820ms on redwood-llm-v1.3.2-std.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood): Hmm, okay. That aligns with our staging runs when KV cache miss rates were high — were you seeing a lot of cache churn?
[00:41] Naomi (Cobalt): Yes, our logs show prefix cache hit was only ~42% during the run, because the customer context varies a lot. For the fallback tiny-latency model we tried, p95 was 210ms but quality dropped on complex instructions.
[00:55] Alex (Redwood): So tradeoff — redwood-llm-v1.3.2 has better quality but higher tail latency when cache misses. tiny-latency-1.0 is fast but lower qa. We need to pin the catalog version for the pilot and define the fallback matrix.
[01:10] Elena (Cobalt): Can you explain pinning vs soft-fallback? I think the product folks want the pinned model to be stable so evaluation metrics are comparable.
[01:18] Priya (Redwood): Absolutely. Pinning means the POC will reference a specific model build (example: redwood-llm-v1.3.2-q4_0). Soft-fallback means at runtime we can route to a compatible variant — e.g. redwood-llm-v1.3.2-quantized or tiny-latency-1.0 — based on policy. Canary is a small fraction, rollback is explicit.
[01:33] Jorge (Cobalt): On the security side, if you automatically fallback to a different variant, does that change our data handling guarantees? We need clarity for our compliance team.
[01:42] Marco (Redwood): Good point — fallback variants inherit the same tenancy and VPC networking; we don't re-route out of the private deployment. However, if a fallback variant is hosted on a different infra tier (e.g., dedicated shared vs private on-prem), we flag that. For this pilot everything stays in the customer's private pool.
[01:59] Samir (Cobalt): Ok, can you list which variants we should consider pinning to?
[02:05] Priya (Redwood): Based on your workload we recommend three candidates: redwood-llm-v1.3.2-std (best quality), redwood-llm-v1.3.2-q4_0 (quantized, ~1.8x cheaper, slight latency gain), tiny-latency-1.0 (fast fallback, lower quality). Also a model we call safety-rerank-v0.9 for post-processing.
[02:26] Naomi (Cobalt): About q4_0 — last week's notes said generation quality regressed on long-form summarization. Did you tweak any attention kernels?
[02:33] Priya (Redwood): We adjusted kernel selection heuristics; q4_0 tends to prefer different memory paths which can change token streaming slightly. That showed up as paraphrase differences in your eval set.
[02:44] Alex (Redwood): We're going to include a regression alert that triggers if Rouge/Lexical F1 drops >3% when rolling.
[02:51] Elena (Cobalt): Good. Back to fallback matrix — what triggers a fallback? High p95? Error rate? Latency threshold?
[02:59] Marco (Redwood): The runtime supports policy by: latency SLO breach (p95 > 750ms sustained for X min), error rate (5xx > 0.5%), or capacity limits. For your pilot we suggested: p95 > 700ms for 2 consecutive minutes triggers soft-fallback to quantized variant, p95 > 1s triggers fallback to tiny-latency.
[03:21] Samir (Cobalt): That seems aggressive but safe. How do we test rollback?
[03:27] Priya (Redwood): We can run a rollback drill: schedule a simulated canary where 5% of traffic routes to a new build for 30 minutes, run your eval prompts automatically, then flip back and validate metrics. We'll do this in staging first.
[03:40] Elena (Cobalt): Who owns the canary run? We need to make sure our PMs are in the loop.
[03:46] Alex (Redwood): Redwood will trigger the canary and share a run-book; Cobalt will validate outputs and metrics. We'll record it and run the rollback if regression.
[03:54] Jorge (Cobalt): On compliance — we need KMS key mapping and audit logs for each model version. Does pinning map to a specific key rotation policy?
[04:03] Marco (Redwood): Pinning doesn't change KMS usage; the same key policy applies. We will include explicit model version metadata in audit logs. We'll share an example log snippet after the call.
[04:14] Naomi (Cobalt): A few quirky transcription notes — some of our log lines are being parsed wrong; the console shows 'K V cash' sometimes in the tokenization view. Not a blocker but odd.
[04:25] Priya (Redwood): Ha, that's the speech-to-text for KV cache. We'll ignore that.
[04:30] Samir (Cobalt): More detail on the benchmark: we measured tokens-per-second and cost per 1k tokens. redwood-llm-v1.3.2-std cost = $6.20 per 1k (hosted equivalent), q4_0 = $3.40 per 1k, tiny-latency = $2.10 per 1k. These numbers help our procurement forecast.
[04:50] Alex (Redwood): Good. For the pilot we usually recommend locking to a single pinned variant for at least 2 weeks so your evals are stable; enable soft-fallback policies for safety, and schedule a canary for any new model build.
[05:05] Elena (Cobalt): What's the simplest pinning config in the console?
[05:09] Priya (Redwood): In Console -> Models -> Pin Version: select model ID, choose canary % (0 if none), rollout window, and fallback rules. We can pre-populate a recommended config and push it as a JSON you can import.
[05:22] Samir (Cobalt): Please do. Also we'd like to see token-level cost breakdown and per-route p95 in the same dashboard.
[05:29] Priya (Redwood): Those dashboards exist — we'll share permalinks to your pilot dashboards and add the token-cost column.
[05:36] Elena (Cobalt): On success criteria, we proposed: 1) p95 < 700ms for core flows, 2) quality delta < 2% vs baseline on eval set, 3) cost below our target $4.5 per 1k. Are we on track?
[05:49] Samir (Cobalt): Right now cost is a bit high on the std build. If q4_0 hits quality thresholds we could switch and stay under cost target.
[05:58] Alex (Redwood): For the pilot, let's plan: pin to redwood-llm-v1.3.2-std today for evaluation, enable soft-fallback to redwood-llm-v1.3.2-q4_0 at p95 > 700ms, and fallback to tiny-latency at p95 > 1s. Schedule canary of v1.3.3 next Thursday.
[06:15] Elena (Cobalt): Can we get the regression alert and the canary playbook in writing?
[06:19] Marco (Redwood): Yes, I'll drop a Playbook doc and the alert rule JSON.
[06:24] Jorge (Cobalt): Also need SOC2 artifact mapping — which of your docs map to our control set?
[06:30] Tara (Redwood): I can send the SOC2/ISO checklist and the pilot-specific audit log example.
[06:34] Samir (Cobalt): One more technical — when you fallback, do you preserve KV cache affinity or does the new variant warm independently?
[06:41] Priya (Redwood): Cache is per model binary and isn't shared across incompatible variants. For compatible variants (same major/model family) we can share prefix/KV caches; we'll list compatibility matrix. So transition cost may include a temporary spike while q4_0 warms.
[06:58] Naomi (Cobalt): That warming behavior may explain the p95 spikes we've seen during switches. Good to know.
[07:04] Alex (Redwood): Ok time check — we have about 50 minutes left. Any blockers?
[07:08] Elena (Cobalt): Nothing blocking. Just confirm the timeline for the end-to-end benchmark.
[07:12] Priya (Redwood): We'll run a 24-hour end-to-end benchmark starting Saturday 00:00 UTC, capturing p50/p95, error rates, and Rouge/Lexical F1 on your eval set. We'll post the full CSV and a short summary.
[07:24] Samir (Cobalt): Can you also include per-tenant breakdown? We want to see which user cohorts cause worst cache churn.
[07:29] Priya (Redwood): Yes, per-tenant and per-route.
[07:32] Alex (Redwood): Next, a quick discussion on rollback sequencing: manual rollback vs automatic fallback.
[07:36] Marco (Redwood): Our recommendation: automatic soft-fallback for short incidents; explicit manual rollback for any regression in quality metrics. We won't auto-roll back model versions without a manual approval gate.
[07:49] Elena (Cobalt): Sounds good. For the canary next week — what data do you need from our side?
[07:54] Priya (Redwood): The eval prompt set and the success thresholds. You already gave the eval set; confirm threshold values and the target canary percentage (we suggested 5%).
[08:03] Elena (Cobalt): Confirmed: 5% canary, thresholds as discussed.
[08:07] Samir (Cobalt): One operational ask — if we pin a version, can we also export a signed artifact that proves which model binary was used for an inference? For audits.
[08:17] Marco (Redwood): Yes, we have deterministic model-build IDs and we can surface the model-binary SHA in logs; we'll add an example signed artifact workflow.
[08:27] Alex (Redwood): All right, let's go through agreed next steps and owners.
[08:31] Elena (Cobalt): Before we do, Jorge — anything else from security?
[08:34] Jorge (Cobalt): No, just timeline on audit logs. If you can send the sample log and KMS mapping today, that's perfect.
[08:42] Alex (Redwood): Great. Quick recap then — we'll pin to redwood-llm-v1.3.2-std, enable quantized soft-fallback and tiny-latency emergency fallback, run 24-hour benchmark starting Saturday, schedule a 5% canary of v1.3.3 next Thursday, and Redwood to send SOC2 artifacts + playbook.
[08:58] Priya (Redwood): Thanks everyone. We'll post the benchmark plan and the console config JSON in the Slack channel and Asana ticket.
[09:08] Samir (Cobalt): Thanks — appreciate it.
[09:10] Alex (Redwood): End.
